docs: credit Audiee.ai in the README footer (en + zh-CN)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

security: localhost-only dashboard by default, access token off loopback, run_command opt-in when exposed (#58)

* security: gate run_command on dashboard exposure, default web bind to loopback

run_command executed shell=True behind a regex denylist and was always in
PRIMITIVE_TOOLS, so anyone who could reach the web agent had a shell. The
denylist stays as defence in depth, but the tool is now authorization-gated:

- config.web_host() defaults to 127.0.0.1 (was 0.0.0.0) with HERANDHIM_WEB_HOST
  override; is_loopback_host()/web_is_loopback() classify the bind.
- config.run_command_enabled(): tools.runCommand / HERANDHIM_TOOLS_RUN_COMMAND,
  explicit true/false, or "auto" = on only while the dashboard is loopback-only.
- Agent._build_tools() withholds the schema and the system prompt stops
  advertising it when disabled; tools.run_command() itself refuses before
  the denylist so a hallucinated call can't slip through.

Co-authored-by: Eric Wang <wangchen2007915@gmail.com>

* security: shared access token for the web dashboard, fail closed off loopback

/ws/chat accepted every connection and no REST route checked anything, so
a published port 7788 was an unauthenticated agent with shell access.

- web/access.py: WebAuth policy from web.accessToken /
  HERANDHIM_WEB_ACCESS_TOKEN; a non-loopback bind without a token raises
  WebAuthError and `herandhim start` exits 2 instead of serving. With a
  token, a pure-ASGI middleware gates every /api/* route and the WebSocket
  (Bearer header or HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie, compared constant-time).
  WebSocket handshakes from a foreign browser Origin are refused even on an
  open loopback install (no CORS for WS). /healthz is the only stateless
  unauthenticated probe.
- /api/access/{status,unlock,lock}: the browser exchanges the token once
  for the cookie; index.html shows a token prompt when required and re-checks
  access before every socket reconnect. Loopback with no token stays open.
- /api/identity hides run_command when it is withheld.
- Wizard and example config default web.host to 127.0.0.1.
- tests/test_web_access.py covers bind default, fail-closed start, 401s on
  every sensitive GET/POST/DELETE, WS rejection, cookie flow, origin check,
  and run_command gating.

Co-authored-by: Eric Wang <wangchen2007915@gmail.com>

* deploy: publish 7788 to localhost only, always token-gate the container, Fly probes /healthz

The container binds 0.0.0.0 and cannot tell whether its port was published
to 127.0.0.1 or the world, so render_config.py now guarantees a token:
HERANDHIM_WEB_ACCESS_TOKEN wins, a saved one is kept, and a fresh install
mints a random one (printed in the log on every boot, file chmod 600).
HERANDHIM_TOOLS_RUN_COMMAND maps onto tools.runCommand for the shell opt-in.

docker-compose and every documented docker run use 127.0.0.1:7788:7788;
fly.toml documents the secret and health-checks /healthz since /api/status
is now gated.

Co-authored-by: Eric Wang <wangchen2007915@gmail.com>

* docs: dashboard exposure rules — loopback default, token off-loopback, run_command opt-in

README (en/zh), deploy README, SECURITY.md and SAFETY.md describe the new
model and the migration for existing web.host: 0.0.0.0 configs; landing
page one-liners publish to 127.0.0.1.

Co-authored-by: Eric Wang <wangchen2007915@gmail.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commit.message:
feat(tts): local text-to-speech (Piper/Kokoro) and reply-in-kind voice replies (#55)

- core/tts.py mirrors core/stt.py: tts.provider auto|elevenlabs|local
  (HERANDHIM_TTS_PROVIDER), local Piper default with auto-downloaded
  zh_CN-huayan-medium voice, optional Kokoro engine, ffmpeg WAV->OGG/Opus
  for Telegram voice notes
- reply-in-kind: inbound Telegram voice notes get voice replies when a TTS
  provider is usable (channels.telegram.replyInKindVoice false|true|auto,
  auto default with voiceReplyMaxChars + tiny-ack probability caps);
  any TTS miss silently falls back to text
- outbound send_voice path: TelegramBot.send_voice, a voice sender wired
  into core/tools with a new send_voice tool (falls back to send_file)
- tts skill (speak.py) gains --engine auto|local following tts.provider;
  gTTS kept only as documented last resort
- optional dep: pip install "herandhim[tts-local]" (not in [all], like
  stt-local); Docker env plumbing (HERANDHIM_TTS_PROVIDER etc.)
- tests with mocked Piper/Kokoro/ffmpeg; README + zh-CN + example JSON

Co-authored-by: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commit.message:
feat(stt): local speech-to-text via faster-whisper as a Deepgram alternative (#54)

Voice notes no longer require sending audio to Deepgram. A new
stt.provider setting (auto | deepgram | local, env HERANDHIM_STT_PROVIDER)
selects the engine behind the existing transcribe_bytes_async interface,
so Telegram and the web dashboard both pick it up unchanged.

- auto (default): Deepgram when a key is set — existing users see no
  change — otherwise local faster-whisper when installed; local also
  covers for Deepgram when the cloud call fails.
- local: audio never leaves the machine. Opt-in extra:
  pip install "herandhim[stt-local]" (kept out of [all] so the default
  Docker image stays lean). Model size / device / computeType / language
  configurable under stt.local; the loaded model is cached.
- Missing-dependency and no-key hints now explain both paths.
- Docker env passthrough (HERANDHIM_STT_PROVIDER / _STT_LOCAL_MODEL),
  example config, .env.example, and both READMEs updated. STT only —
  no TTS / voice replies.

Co-authored-by: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commit.message:
feat(memory): overnight quiet-hours memory consolidation (opt-in) (#53)

Adds a nightly batch pass over the Markdown memory stores, reusing the
write-time Mem0-lite helpers (find_similar + decide) from #52: recently
updated entries are merged against the rest of the store, invalidated
entries are moved to ARCHIVE.md (never hard-deleted), and optional
age-based soft decay archives entries untouched for N days.

- Registered on the shared APScheduler at 03:30 local (hour tunable via
  memory.overnightHour) only when memory.overnightConsolidation is true
  (or HERANDHIM_MEMORY_OVERNIGHT_CONSOLIDATION=true) — off by default.
- PROTECTED_KEYS are never scanned, never shown to the LLM as targets,
  and never archived.
- Live agents' in-memory MemoryStorage objects are consolidated directly
  so a later write can't resurrect archived entries.
- Per-store nightly LLM budget; every failure is a logged no-op that
  leaves MEMORY.md intact; short report in the daemon log and
  context/logs/overnight_consolidation.md.
- Markdown stays the source of truth — no graph store, no extra DB.

Co-authored-by: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>
